quick.summary: How to make sure users see critical information first.
quick.takeaway: Make the most important thing look the most important.

beats.line: People ignore the warning on my screen. They just hit submit. Why?
Because the submit button is the loudest thing there. What catches your eye first?
Think of a road sign. The speed limit is huge. The seal is tiny.
Because the speed limit is what you actually need to see.
Exactly. We usually call this visual hierarchy.
Can I just say guide the eye with size?
Absolutely. Guide the eye with size.
If the warning matters most, make it bolder than the button.
So I should make the warning text larger and the button smaller.
Make the most important thing look the most important.

quiz.question: You want users to notice a critical error message. How should you format it?
options: Make it visually heavier than the elements around it.
Place it at the very bottom of the page.
Use the exact same font size as the body text.
Remove all other buttons from the screen.
quiz.explanation: Using size and weight naturally draws the eye before anything else.

quiz.question: Every item on a screen should grab the user's attention equally.
quiz.explanation: If everything shouts, nothing is heard. You must guide the eye with size and contrast.
